notes: Static sibling of name(); the pair reads name()/legacy_name().

Returns subscriber id => attempts for one event. Not failed(): the ledger's delivered()/exhausted() are bool predicates on a (subscriber, event) pair, so a bare failed($event_id) returning a map would read as a third predicate.

mark_failed() plus the redelivery args; 'For' named nothing. Assumes core-outbox-delivery maps IDeliveryLedger::markFailed -> mark_failed (0.6 vocabulary). Alternative the operator may prefer: drop this method and give WpDeliveryLedger::mark_failed() an optional trailing ?array $redelivery = null (PHP allows an implementation to add optional params); that is a signature change, not a rename.

reason: Reads as a sentence with its $reason arg and says what differs from mark_exhausted(); '_with' would be ambiguous next to mark_failed_with(redelivery).

notes: Returns an int (count of the private orphans() list); the current name reads as if it returned the redeliveries. Pairs with the existing private orphans().
Matches the *_of lookup style other areas use (event_id_of, status_of).
Bare register() would blur with bind(); the object is a consumer config.

reason: The _for_tests suffix is a deliberate test-seam warning shared across areas (HostDefaults, InMemory* *ForTests); keep it so the seam stays obvious at call sites.
notes: Assumes core-effects maps HostDefaults::resetForTests -> reset_for_tests and the other *ForTests seams keep the suffix. If the operator rules seams go bare (reset()), apply the same to both wp seams.
Static derivation of the deterministic id from (hook, kind, callable); a noun is right for 'the id of this callable'.
Zero call sites in any corpus; candidate for removal rather than rename (operator call).

reason: The 'or held by this connection' half is the whole point (the WP8-10 repair guard holds the lock itself); 'mine' is the shortest word that keeps it. Inverting to is_held_elsewhere would flip the fail-closed default on a query error, so it is not a pure rename.

notes: Same concept as PdoPauseStore::activePatterns and DbalRelayPauseStore::activePatterns (pdo, symfony areas). IRelayPauseStore::hold()/release() call the thing a 'selector', so I recommend all three converge on active_selectors; if those areas pick active_patterns (or a bare active()), this should follow them instead.
Sibling properties are single words (relay, reprojected, stranded, errors); restored parallels reprojected. Promoted ctor param: any named-argument call (redeliveriesRestored:) must follow.
Count of pending by-reference integration actions due after now; sits beside pending() in the drain's 'remaining' sum.
Takes the \wpdb and inspects its last error; same concept as IHostConnection::isDuplicateKey (pdo area), assumed to become is_duplicate_key. 'last error' is implied by the wpdb argument.
Siblings are minted, running, exhausted. Promoted ctor param: named-argument calls must follow.

Callback of the {prefix}_ddd_wakeup hook for WakeKind::ResumeRetry intents; keeps the wake kind's name. Assumes core-process maps WakeupIntent::resumeRetry -> resume_retry so the kind has one spelling.

reason: Same test-seam suffix rule as WpLedgeredDelivery::reset_for_tests.

notes: Shared with IntegrationDelivery, WakeRetryPolicy, ProcessWakeupHandler and Relay backoffSeconds (core-outbox, core-process, symfony). The unit stays in the name (the constants say _SECONDS and the callers add it to timestamps). All five should land on one name; if the operator shortens to backoff(), this follows.
begin() for one intent by idempotency key; pairs with finish_key. The string 'beginKey' is also the write() label in an error message (string_refs=1); update it with the rename.
finish() by key. 'finishKey' also appears as write() labels in error messages (string_refs=3); update them with the rename.

reason: Same name as PdoJobStore::hasLiveIntent (pdo area), assumed to become has_live_intent; 'live' (pending or firing) is the specific state.
Counterpart of has_live_intent on the same scheduler; the pair should read alike.
